Function documentation:
[
  {
    "application_scenario": "Used to initialize a Parser object from a memory buffer before subsequent parsing operations such as parser_next.",
    "example_code": "Parser parser;\nconst unsigned char buf[] = {0x01, 0x02, 0x03};\nint rc = parser_from_memory(&parser, buf, sizeof(buf));\nif (rc != 0) {\n    /* handle error */\n}",
    "function": "parser_from_memory",
    "function_id": "src/parser.c:3:parser_from_memory",
    "functionality": "Initializes a Parser from an in-memory buffer. If size is zero, returns -1 without modifying the parser. Otherwise, sets parser->state to the first byte of data and returns 0.",
    "notes": [
      "Only the first byte of data is used to initialize parser->state.",
      "The Parser struct is expected to have a state field.",
      "Related functions include parser_next, node_process, and parser_free."
    ],
    "parameter_notes": [
      "parser: non-const pointer to a Parser struct; written to via parser->state.",
      "data: const pointer to the input byte buffer; only data[0] is read when size > 0.",
      "size: number of bytes in data; must be > 0 for successful initialization."
    ],
    "resource_lifecycle_notes": [
      "Does not allocate or free memory.",
      "Caller is responsible for the lifetime of the Parser and data buffer.",
      "Parser should be released via parser_free when no longer needed."
    ],
    "return_semantics": "Returns 0 on success (size > 0), -1 if size == 0.",
    "signature": "int parser_from_memory( Parser *parser, const unsigned char *data, unsigned long size);"
  }
]
